messages:
maya: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread — I want to lock down the runtime <-> policy engine contract before we start the adapter refactor. TL;DR: we should keep policy evaluation pure (no runtime calls) and have the runtime do final route scoring with a small 'compat' shim. Thoughts?
aj: +1 to purity. Keeping evaluation pure makes it testable and cacheable. main question: what inputs does the policy evaluator need? latency_slo_ms? effective_cost_budget? region_hardset vs region_hint?
maya: Right — propose the evaluator receives a normalized RequestContext: tenant_id, model_family, prompt_shape (tokens, seq_len_p50/p95), latency_slo_ms (nullable), cost_budget_micros (nullable), region_preferences (ordered list), tier (free/prod/enterprise), and recent_error_rate. It returns a list of candidate route descriptors with soft penalties and explicit hard filters.
chris: I like candidate descriptors with soft penalties. Implementation detail: runtime needs to know if a candidate is "route-compatible" at call time — e.g., model variant exists on node, quantized fallback OK, accepts streaming. So descriptor should include capability flags. Also we should surface a numeric penalty and a reason string. Example: {route, penalty, capability_mask, region, estimated_p99_ms}.
sam: Concern: where do we compute estimated_p99_ms and cost estimates? Doing that inside the policy engine could create drift vs runtime telemetry. My vote: evaluator can provide conservative cost/latency estimates (e.g., baseline + penalty), but runtime should override with live telemetry and re-score while honoring hard filters from policy.
lina: How do we express hard constraints vs soft penalties in the contract? We need a small DSL: allow filters like region == eu (hard), max_latency <= 200ms (soft with huge penalty if violated), tier == enterprise (hard). Might be a list of {type: "filter" | "soft", expression}.
aj: Agreed. Filter objects for hard gating; penalty objects for rank adjustments. Also we should keep the serializer stable to allow cache keys. PolicyEvalRequest -> deterministic candidate list. Runtime scoring runs: final_score = base_penalty + runtime_penalty + telemetry_adjustment. If final_score > threshold => reject.
maya: Two more practical constraints: 1) keep policy evaluation cheap so it can run synchronously at API gateway (we can't call the full model catalog or heavy datastore). 2) ensure fallbacks are explicit (if primary excluded, candidate list should include next N).
chris: For 1) we'd precompute and regularly refresh a compact model-catalog snapshot (model_id -> static capabilities + typical_cost_ms/10k_tokens). Policy engine uses that snapshot. For 2) include a prioritized candidate list length param. Also add an "allow_fallbacks" flag per tenant.
sam: Edge case: tenant-specific affinity/sharding (dedicated pools). The policy evaluator must be able to express tenancy pins as hard filters (tenant_pool == pool-42). But we should avoid baking runtime topology into policy — keep it as a tag the runtime resolves.
lina: Tests: we need unit tests that assert evaluator determinism, and integration tests where runtime re-scores and we assert that per-tenant SLOs hold under synthetic load. Also capture telemetry signals used for re-scoring: recent_p95, node_queue_ms, model_jitter, request_size_norm.
maya: On tie-breakers: prefer deterministic stable ordering over random jitter; use (score, last_seen_success_ts desc, capacity_score desc). This avoids flapping when telemetry noisy.
aj: Also consider circuit-breaker state: runtime should send back circuit info to policy refresher for next eval window so policy can temporarily deprioritize nodes with active circuits. But keep that async.
chris: Implementation plan: 1) define PolicyEvalRequest/Response proto + JSON mapping. 2) build lightweight model-catalog snapshot pubsub. 3) implement evaluator service (k8s) and a small gateway lib that calls it with RequestContext. 4) implement runtime shim that consumes candidate descriptors and re-scores with live telemetry.
maya: Backwards compat: old clients expect route strings. We will support a compat mode where evaluator returns a single best-route string and runtime treats it as a hint. Deprecate after 3 months.
sam: Ops note: instrument every decision point with trace tags: policy_id, candidate_count, chosen_route, final_score, telemetry_adjustment. That'll help debug regressions.
lina: Security/compliance: policy engine must never leak private tenant attributes in candidate reason strings. Use opaque codes instead of free-text where tenant_id shows up.
aj: runtime will enforce that when logging.
deploy-bot: deploy "policy-eval-service v0.1.0" for staging completed by @chris — see https://deploys.redwood.internal/2345 :rocket:
maya: Next steps: @chris to draft proto schema by EOD Friday, @aj to outline caching/TTL semantics, @lina to write test plan, @sam to add telemetry signals list. Catch-up Wednesday 10am PT. :calendar:
